@@U00306@@
And yet there’s another way to satisfy this want.
We learn to prize the things of the spirit,
to long for revelation which nowhere burns more nobly
and with greater beauty than in the New Testament.
I must open that fundamental text;
I must, now, with all honorable dedication,
turn that holy original
into my beloved German.

@@U00307@@
(He opens a large volume and prepares to begin.)

@@U00308@@
It is written:
“In the beginning was the Word!”
Already I’m stuck.
Who will help me?
Who?
Someone!
How can I rate the Word so highly?
I must translate it otherwise
if ’'m truly enlightened by the spirit.
It is written:
“In the beginning was the Mind!”
Not so fast.
Let’s not rush over that first line!
Is it truly the mind that creates all things?
Surely it ought to read:
“In the beginning was the Force!”
And yet I’ve scarcely written it and
immediately something tells me it’s not right.
But, yes, now the spirit’s helping,
helping me,
and all at once I have it, and write:
EEATUS ieee AUREL ONES 49
translation:
@@U00306@@
然而还有另一种方法可以满足这种需求。
我们学会珍视精神的事物，
渴望得到启示，没有什么比这更燃烧的了
并且比新约中的更加美丽。
我必须打开那篇基础文本；
现在，我必须以所有光荣的奉献精神，
转动那神圣的原物
翻译成我心爱的德语。

@@U00307@@
（他打开一本大书，准备开始。）

@@U00308@@
文中写道：
“太初有道！”
我已经被困住了。
谁来帮助我？
WHO？
有人！
我怎么能对神的话语给予如此高的评价呢？
否则我必须翻译它
如果真的受到精神的启发。
文中写道：
“太初是心！”
没那么快。
我们不要急于完成第一行！
真的是心创造了万物吗？
当然，它应该读作：
“一开始就是原力！”
但我几乎还没写完
立刻有什么东西告诉我这是不对的。
但是，是的，现在精神在帮忙，
帮助我，
我一下子就得到了它，并写道：
EEATUS ieee AUREL ONES 49
